title: Kernel arbitration causing attention buffer tiling miswrite and float drift during prefill-decode handover
creator: Maya Chen
description: Intermittent correctness regression observed after shipping the kernel arbitration change that allows the runtime scheduler to preempt long-running fused-attn kernels. Symptoms include miswritten attention buffer tiles during the prefill -> decode handover, followed by small but accumulating floating-point drift that alters token sampling on longer generations. Reproducible on internal stress harness and observed in customer telemetry with long-context summarization jobs. This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, mitigation, and tests to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: Run internal stress harness `tools/runtime-stress --model redwood/open-13b --seq 4096 --prefill-batch 12 --concurrency 8` for 30 minutes
Issue appears ~20-25 minutes into the run as token emulation traces diverge between baseline and optimized runtime
Locally: instrumented run with DEBUG=kernel_scheduling and compare KV/attn buffer checksums before and after kernel handover
Observed customer case: long-context summarization pipeline (seq 6k) with model fallback and opportunistic preemption enabled
observed_behavior: After a preemptive kernel switch during a long prefill, certain attention tile rows are overwritten with shifted offsets. Subsequent decode steps read misaligned KV/attn regions producing small numeric deviations (1e-5 to 1e-3) that accumulate and change greedy/beam selection for tail tokens.
expected_behavior: Kernel arbitration should not cause any writes outside the kernel-owned buffer region. Prefill->decode handover should preserve KV/attn tile boundaries and maintain bitwise-identical outputs compared to baseline when deterministic configuration is used.
root_cause_hypothesis: Race between kernel allocator and the continuous-batching prefetcher: when the scheduler preempts a fused-attn kernel, the allocator reassigns a shared buffer slice for the next kernel without waiting for the in-flight write fence. On FP16 paths the misordered writes manifest as small numerical drift; on quantized paths corruption is more visible. The arbitration code added an optimistic free-before-fence to reduce tail latency, which introduced the window.
investigation_notes: 02/26: Added hardware memory fences around kernel completion; reproducibility dropped but still seen under high concurrency
02/27: Instrumented GPU pointer lifetimes and found ~2.4% of preemptions where a buffer slice was reused before queue memory commit completed
02/28: Confirmed numerical drift is larger when mixed-precision kernel path selected; float32 path shows similar logical misreads but smaller magnitude
03/01: Created minimal reproducer that toggles `runtime.scheduler.optimistic_release` and shows binary-identical outputs when disabled
03/04: A/B test in staging running with optimistic_release=false eliminated the issue in customer-like workloads
03/06: Stress PR introducing explicit cudaStreamSynchronize barriers reduced occurrence but increased latency p95 by ~18% — unacceptable for hosted SLA
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1634 (hotfix: deferred free with per-slice completion tokens)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1641 (stress test added to CI, reproducer harness)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1650 (rollback candidate: revert optimistic_release default to false)
mitigation_plan: Ship PR #1634 which introduces per-slice completion tokens and defers free until hardware-reported done state
Run extended staging soak for 72 hours with production-like concurrency and long-context jobs
Add CI stress job that runs the reproducer nightly on GPU pool with multiple MKL/driver versions
Add runtime flag `scheduler.strict_release` to gate the optimization behind opt-in until proven safe
decision: Apply hotfix PR #1634 to staging and monitor for 72h. Do not enable optimistic_release by default for hosted until downstream quantized paths are validated. Schedule rollback option if any new corruption events are observed in staging.
